title: Gateway Request Simulator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning Record Store
xAPI
Ingestion Gateway
Statement Validation
HTTP
description: A p5.js simulator in which learners build a batch of up to five xAPI statements, set the bearer token and broker state, predict whether the ingestion gateway accepts or rejects the batch, and watch the five request steps return 200, 400 with every violation, 401 or 503 with Retry-After.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: The ingestion gateway's five request steps and the all-or-nothing batch
learningObjectives: The learner will demonstrate the gateway's five request steps and predict whether a batch is accepted or rejected in full.
prerequisites: The parts of an xAPI statement and the three MicroSim verbs (Chapter 16)
The producer contract rules on verbs, results, grouping and page IRIs (Chapter 16)

accessibility.notes: All actions use native buttons, a select and checkboxes; pass and fail are shown with check and cross marks and text as well as color

controls.label: Add broken statement
controls.purpose: Add a card with the chosen defect

controls.label: Predict first
controls.purpose: Require a prediction before the result is revealed

controls.label: Send batch
controls.purpose: Run the batch through the five steps

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Clear the batch and the queue

controls.label: Accepted
controls.purpose: Predict that the batch will be accepted

controls.label: Rejected
controls.purpose: Predict that the batch will be rejected

controls.label: Statement cards
controls.purpose: Remove a card from the batch

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Build a batch, predict the outcome, step through the pipeline, fix and resend
keyQuestions: Why is a batch with one broken statement rejected in full?
Why does authentication come before validation?
When may the gateway answer 503, and why is that the one page-worthy failure?
commonMisconceptions: Valid statements in a rejected batch are stored anyway
The gateway stops at the first violation
A 200 means the statement is already in the analytics database
assessmentOpportunities: Naming the index, field and contract section of each violation
Explaining the order of the five steps

equations: accepted if token valid AND every statement passes the contract AND the queue acknowledges
assumptions: Rules and messages mirror the repository gateway's validation.py and app.py
A down broker is modeled as a local producer queue that fills and cannot drain
limitations: Only four defects and five templates are modeled
Statement ids are illustrative, not real UUIDv7 values
The version-header check is not modeled
